parameters.description: The code from the terminal, or from the link the CLI printed.

get.summary: A secret's restricted flag and access list. Admins only.

patch.summary:
Restricts or unrestricts a secret and changes its access list, all at once. Admins only.
Restricting and granting need the project setting on; unrestricting and revoking always
work, so a project can be cleaned up before the setting is turned off. A restricted secret
is reachable only by the principals on its list, for the actions listed, and only as far as
their roles also allow; admins keep access so a secret is never orphaned.

get.description: Newest first, one page at a time. A page shorter than `limit` is the last; otherwise pass the oldest version returned as `before` for the next.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Versions to return, newest first: 100 by default, at most 200.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only versions older than this one, to fetch the page after one ending at `before`.

requestBody.description: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 512 KiB and 4096 pixels on a side. SVG is refused; convert it to PNG first.

429.description: `rate_limited`, or `logo_busy` while the caller's previous upload is still being processed

get.summary: Admins only, along with the restricted secrets they may see.

put.summary:
Turns per-secret access on or off for the project. It is off by default, and turning it off
is refused while any secret in the project is restricted, so no restriction lapses unnoticed.
The default for every secret in the project that does not set its own. Off unless set.

get.summary: Every readable value under a path, for machines. Secrets the caller cannot read are left out.

post.description: POST, so a browser session needs the CSRF header like any other change.

409.description: `seal_config_tampered`: the seal configuration failed its integrity check, so it is not backed up

429.description: Another backup is running, or this caller has taken six in the last hour

507.description: Too large to back up through the API

post.description: Replaces the root key and re-encrypts every value under it, so the old passphrase opens nothing in the live database. Backups taken earlier still open with the old passphrase. Stored data that no longer decrypts is refused with `unreadable_data`, naming it by id, unless `skip_unreadable` is set.
Open while uninitialised; afterwards only for organisation admins.
Drops the root key from memory. A remembered unlock is kept, so the next restart unlocks itself; forget the unlock as well to stop that.

get.description: Unauthenticated. After setup only `state`, `web_setup` and `version` are filled in; organisation admins get the rest from `/api/v1/sys/status/detail`.
Every status field, including how the server was unlocked and whether an unlock is remembered.

put.description: `remember` and `passphrase-file` need the current passphrase in the body; `manual` does not.

post.description: Answers with the public status. Also served on the host socket, where the network's rate limits do not apply.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text matched against name, email, groups and id.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` is the default for names, `desc` makes sense for dates.

post.summary: Ends the browser session and clears its cookie.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

total.description: Entries matching the filters across all pages.

skip_unreadable.description:
Re-encrypt what can be read and leave values, project keys or stored credentials that no
longer decrypt as they are, auditing each. Without it, the change is refused and the error
lists them.

ClaimBindings.description: Constraints a verified token's claims must satisfy before a machine identity may log in.

claims.description: Claim name (or JSON pointer starting with `/`) to globs; every entry must match.

CliApproveRequest.description: The code the person typed from their own terminal; a code carried in a link is not enough.

CliDenyRequest.description: A CLI login to refuse; the code is typed or carried from the approval page.

Conditions.description: Restrictions on where a rule applies. Empty lists mean "anywhere".

tags.description: Matches when the secret carries any of these tags.

ttl.description: Seconds until the secret stops working, at most ten years; never when absent.

environments.description: Environments to create; defaults to development, staging and production.

client_secret.description: Shown once; only a hash is stored.

GenerateSecret.description: Request to fill a secret with a newly generated value, creating it if needed.

oneOf.description: Overrides the secret's policy generator for this value only.

actions.description: Any of `read`, `read-value`, `edit` and `delete`; `read` is always added.

passphrase.description: Required in passphrase mode; at least 12 characters.

setup_code.description: The one-time code from the server log.

admin_token.description: A short-lived organisation admin token, shown once.

token.description: The OIDC or Kubernetes service account token.

ca_cert.description: PEM CA bundle for the API server.

host.description: API server URL, required for TokenReview.

issuer.description: Service account issuer, required for JWKS mode.

jwks.description: Inline JWKS document, as returned by `kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks`.

max_token_lifetime.description:
Longest service account token accepted, from `iat` to `exp`, in seconds; 3600 when left
out, and at most ten years. Tokens without `iat` are refused. In TokenReview mode it
applies to tokens whose claims can be read.

reviewer_jwt.description:
Token of a service account bound to `system:auth-delegator`. Write-only: reads return
`[redacted]`, and sending that value back keeps the stored token.

logout_url.description: The provider's end-session URL to send the browser to, when it has one.

is_org_admin.description: Holds `org-admin`, the same check the system routes make.

org_roles.description: Organisation role slugs held, including those implied by configuration.

org_rules.description: Organisation-level rules, so clients can hide actions that would be refused.

principal_name.description: Display name for users and identities; the group name for groups.

OidcAuthConfig.description: Machine login using JWTs from any OIDC issuer, such as GitHub Actions or Keycloak service accounts.

jwks_url.description: Overrides discovery when the issuer does not publish `.well-known/openid-configuration`.

max_token_lifetime.description:
Longest token accepted, from `iat` to `exp`, in seconds; 3600 when left out, and at most
ten years. Tokens without `iat` are refused.

environments.description: Environment slug to version, absent where the key is missing.

PassphraseStrength.description: zxcvbn's verdict on a passphrase, from 0 (guessable) to 4.

acceptable.description: Long enough, free of control characters and scores 4.

PendingCliLogin.description: A CLI login waiting for approval, so the person can tell whether they started it.

code_hint.description: Never set by this server: the person must type the whole code from their terminal.

requested_from_ip.description: The client address that started the login, as the server saw it.

same_address.description:
Whether the requester's address matches the address of the browser asking. Behind shared
NAT this can be true for someone else, and a VPN can make it false for the same person.

user_agent.description: Reported by the requester, so it can be faked.

PolicyOverride.description: A secret's own setting: follow the project, or use `policy` (which may switch everything off).

logo_url.description: Versioned URL of the project's logo, absent when it has none.

secret_access.description: Secrets here may be restricted to their own access lists.

manages_secret_access.description:
The caller is a project or organisation admin, so manages per-secret access and is
exempt from access lists, though not from their own rules.

path.description: Restrict the restore to this folder and everything beneath it.

SealMode.description: How the root key is kept between restarts.

SealState.description: Whether the server can reach its secrets.

generated.description: The current value was generated by sekret, so rotation may replace it.

next_rotation_at.description: When automatic rotation will next replace the value; absent when rotation does not apply.

restricted.description: Only principals on its access list, and admins, may reach it.

value.description: Absent when the caller may see the key but not its value, or did not ask for values.

SecretAccess.description: Who may reach a secret beyond its role rules.

restricted.description:
Only principals on `grants`, project admins and organisation admins may reach it, and
only as far as their roles also allow. Off, the list has no effect.

SecretAccessChange.description: Changes to one secret's access, applied together.

grant.description: Entries to add, or to replace the actions of for a principal already listed.

restricted.description: Restricting needs the project setting on.

Every restricted secret in the project the caller's roles let them see, deleted ones
included. The setting cannot be turned off while any secret is restricted.

restricted_count.description: Restricted secrets in the project, including any the caller's roles hide.

SecretGrant.description: One entry on a secret's access list.

principal_name.description: Display name for users and identities; the group name for groups.

SecretPolicy.description: How a secret's value is produced and refreshed. Both parts off is the default.

oneOf.description: How sekret generates the value; `None` uses the default (32 alphanumeric) when asked to generate.

rotation_days.description: Days between automatic rotations; `None` turns rotation off.

SecretPolicyView.description: A secret's own policy setting together with what actually applies to it.

restricted.description:
`true` creates the secret restricted, with an empty access list, so it is never open
even for a moment; that needs a project admin and the project setting on. For a secret
that already exists it must match whether it is restricted, which only the access
route changes.

passphrase.description:
The current passphrase; required for `remember` and `passphrase-file`, which weaken how
the server is unlocked.

changes.description: What restoring this snapshot would change.

SysStatus.description:
`GET /sys/status` answers without authentication, so monitoring can alert on a sealed server,
and then fills in only `state`, `web_setup` and `version`, plus what configuration has decided
while uninitialised. `GET /sys/status/detail` fills in every field for organisation admins.

configured.description: The unlock policy comes from server configuration and cannot be changed through the API.

remember_available.description:
The configuration sets `seal.remember_file`, so the remember policy can be chosen. Shown
before setup and to organisation admins.

remembered.description:
A remembered unlock is in place, so the next start unlocks itself. Sealing by hand does not
clear it; forget the unlock for that.

oneOf.description: Once initialised, the stored mode. Before that, the mode the configuration requires, if any.

How the server is unlocked after a start; passphrase mode only. Before setup, the policy
the configuration sets, if any.

How the root key got into memory, while unsealed. `key-file` with a passphrase `seal_mode`
means a root key file overrode the passphrase.

web_setup.description: First-boot setup is offered through the API and web interface.

UnlockPolicy.description: How a passphrase-mode server gets unlocked after it starts.

UnsealedBy.description: How the root key got into memory this time.
